scope: Globally diverse evidence and mapping disposition for Africa, the Americas and Oceania. Existing packets are referenced rather than overwritten; new Ethiopian and West African records are explicitly rejected until a bounded population interval and EU5 crosswalk can be produced.

promotion_audit.decision: No candidate in this wave meets every two-sided scale-anchor criterion. Mapungubwe, Great Zimbabwe and Tongatapu remain vetted one-sided lower bounds in existing packets. Rapa Nui, Maya, Titicaca, Samoa, Tahiti, Nukunonu and Cahokia remain validation-only or unresolved. Hohokam remains a lower-bound test but the current accepted p50 is below its 53,000-person floor. Ethiopian highland and broad West African cases are rejected because the surviving evidence is qualitative, urban/polity-wide, or lacks a defensible mapped interval.
minimum_scale_anchor_requirements_checke: mappable historical boundary with quantified EU5 coverage
defensible population interval for that same boundary
trade, urban, migration, war, epidemic and census caveats resolved

records.label: Lasta/Lalibela Ethiopian highlands medieval landscape
pressure_evidence: Finneran (Azania 47, 2012) reports that Lalibela is described as a medieval capital but that focused archaeological research remains limited; the survey is not a population enumeration.

The Lalibela landscape survey records medieval settlement remains and extensive agricultural exploitation, grazing and tree cutting, but does not publish a contemporaneous population interval or a saturation fraction.

FAO's Ethiopian-highlands synthesis describes grain, enset and livestock systems and severe long-run soil, water and forest pressure, but its modern development evidence cannot be back-cast as a 1337 label.
records.boundary_description: Potential Lasta/Lalibela archaeological survey zone in the Ethiopian highlands; no complete historical rural polygon is supplied by the cited survey.
records.boundary_source: Finneran 2012 Lalibela landscape survey; no population-boundary polygon available
records.source_family_independence: The archaeological survey and FAO agroecological synthesis are treated as one qualitative evidence family; neither supplies a usable medieval population label.
records.notes: Retain as a research lead and qualitative physical-feature check only. Do not infer a population interval from church scale, modern Ethiopian population pressure, or the broad Zagwe/Solomonic polity.

records.label: Inland Niger Delta and Togué/Jenne regional settlement systems
pressure_evidence: Jousse et al. (Proceedings of the Prehistoric Society) report thousands of tell-like dwelling mounds, fertile pasture/cultivation/fishing preferences, and high population densities in the Inland Niger Delta, but do not provide a complete 1100-1450 population interval for a mapped boundary.

The West African land-use atlas (Journal of World Prehistory, 2019) documents diversified farming, rice systems, fishing and changing floodplain use through AD 1500; it is a food-system source, not a population census.

McIntosh and McIntosh's Jenne-jeno estimate peaks in AD 750-1100 and is already retained in `africa_jenne_jeno_regional_validation_wave22.json`; its city/market cluster and pre-1337 date prevent promotion here.
The Togué and Inland Delta literature notes trade-route changes and socio-political instability in the fifteenth century, making a single equilibrium interpretation unsafe.
records.trade_dependence: mixed_to_high for non-food goods and market exchange; staple rice, millet/sorghum, fish and cattle are locally evidenced
records.boundary_description: Potential Inland Niger Delta/Togué survey region in Mali; published descriptions identify a broad alluvial region but do not supply one complete historical aggregate polygon for 1100-1450.
records.boundary_source: Jousse et al. regional surveys; Dueppen 2016 West African archaeology overview
records.source_family_independence: Regional archaeology and land-use synthesis are treated as one family; the existing Jenne-jeno population estimate is not counted as a new independent 1337 group.
records.notes: Do not use Mali/Ghana/Songhai empire area or city population figures as local capacity labels. A future candidate would need a georeferenced floodplain survey unit, dated settlement counts and independent local-food pressure evidence.

records.label: Mapungubwe bounded survey landscape
records.boundary_description: Mapungubwe National Park and UNESCO buffer survey footprint; see existing packet.
records.notes: Existing vetted one-sided floor only; not a two-sided scale anchor because the terminal drought and archaeological reconstruction prevent saturation inference.

records.label: Great Zimbabwe archaeological site
records.boundary_description: Great Zimbabwe National Monument archaeological site; see existing packet.
records.notes: Existing conservative floor only; city/urban hinterland distinction and conflicting population reconstructions block two-sided use.

records.label: Cahokia/American Bottom regional archaeology
records.boundary_description: Cahokia core plus proposed American Bottom hinterland; the existing packet has no EU5 crosswalk.
records.notes: Population and pressure evidence are strong enough for a future regional validation, but mapping is zero-coverage; city estimates cannot be assigned to the surrounding EU5 location.

records.label: Hohokam Lower Salt River/Phoenix Basin canal corridor
records.boundary_description: Lower Salt canal-community study corridor; see existing lower-bound packet.
records.notes: Existing 53,000-person physical/historical floor. The current accepted p50 sum for guwevkabaya+yavpe is 41,132, so this is a useful failing lower-bound diagnostic, not a scale anchor.

records.label: Classic Maya central lowlands LiDAR reconstruction
records.boundary_description: 95,000 km2 LiDAR/archaeological footprint; out of period.
records.notes: Held out because the population peak is 600-900 CE, not 1337, and the footprint is only 86% mapped.

records.label: Tiwanaku raised-field sustaining area
records.boundary_description: Three documented raised-field valleys; see existing packet.
records.notes: Explicit agricultural potential, not observed saturation; useful to test terrace/frost/water mechanics only.

records.label: Rapa Nui island food-limited demographic model
records.boundary_description: Entire Rapa Nui island and nearshore food system.
records.notes: Food-limited model and strong pressure evidence, but estimates are highly assumption-sensitive and post-date/extend beyond 1337; held out.

records.label: Tongatapu island locally supported population floor
records.boundary_description: Entire Tongatapu island; existing crosswalk covers 97.64% of cited area.
records.notes: One-sided floor only; competing 50,000-60,000 LiDAR reconstruction is retained as disagreement, not silently merged.

records.label: Upolu/Samoa pre-contact population reconstruction
records.boundary_description: Entire Upolu island; existing packet assigns 75,400 of the Samoa reconstruction to Upolu.
records.notes: Date starts near 1400 and population is reconstructed; use as held-out island pressure/density test only.

records.label: Tahiti pre-contact population reconstruction
records.boundary_description: Entire Tahiti island; existing packet covers 99.63% of cited area.
records.notes: Contact-era reconstruction and outside 1337; held out despite strong local-food and pressure evidence.

records.label: Nukunonu/Tokelau atoll hostile-island analogue
records.boundary_description: Nukunonu atoll; existing packet maps the named island tag but the observation is modern.
records.notes: Hostile freshwater-limited island test only; modern trade and demography make it unusable for 1337 training.

current_model_snapshot.metric: accepted raw capacity_people_p50; values are diagnostics, not training labels
current_model_snapshot.interpretation: Mapungubwe and Great Zimbabwe p50 values exceed conservative site floors, while Hohokam fails its published lower-bound test. Cahokia's apparent 27-68x excess is not an admissible model error because its historical boundary has zero EU5 coverage; the current single-location capacity cannot be compared to a regional American Bottom interval.

next_mapping_tasks: Do not map Lasta/Lalibela or Inland Niger Delta polity areas to one EU5 location until historical rural boundaries are reconstructed.
Resolve the Cahokia/American Bottom regional polygon and EU5 intersection before comparing capacities.
Retain Hohokam's mapped canal corridor as a failing one-sided test and audit irrigation area, water budget and selected EU5 footprint before changing shared parameters.
Keep city/port cores (Great Zimbabwe, Jenne, Timbuktu, Cahokia core, Lalibela) separate from rural food catchments.
Promote no record to global scale from this wave.
